Central Ohio Regional Qualifier 2014
Newark, OH, USA
June 8th, 2014

Darby Keeney

Deck Name : (2014) Replay Value
Author : Darby Keeney
Description : This deck is about as toolboxy as I get. Minion text offers on-demand bleed and Orlando almost ensures votelock, so the deck is often able make opportunistic moves.

The finals saw 4 of the 5 players in potentialliy winning positions as the clock wore down. This created incentive for an unusual number of cross-table rescues, allowing me to survive Hugh's relentless Ahrimane and Ossian rushing. I got a lucky VP in the end for a win as high seed.

Messages.Author: TryDeflectingThisGrapple
Messages.Body:
> KevinM wrote:
> I dislike the prayer Legendary Vampire, as it's nearly always a discard.
>
You're free to dislike it, but in my experience it is never discarded without a specific intent to Tablet it back. It's both exceedingly strong and self-protecting with Orlando in play.

This Orlando variant tends to create a new minion every time a Villein flows into hand. The result is that fresh minions pop into play at seemingly odd times, which preserves the value of a mid-game Legendary. So where you see a discard, I see opportunity.

In other decks like this which are more Banish-focused, I have self-Banished a tapped, nearly full minion because a Legendary flowed into hand during an active turn - it was worth that much to me.

Ultimately, I believe it's too good to omit from a deck with a reasonable probability of seeing Orlando.

Messages.Author: kombainas
Messages.Body:
I have to agree, Legendary Vampire does not have to be played as a prayer card. If you plan to bring 7+ vamps mid-to-late game, you would probably have it by then and it would be stronger than any average card you would cycle through. The card is tricky to play, but great when you know what you are doing.

Sabbat. If this vampire's bleed is successful, he laughs manicly and untaps.
